competitive_landscape: Local diesel water-taxis and hotel dhows handle nearly all current archipelago transport. SafariLink and Skyward Express run the air gateway to Manda. No electric / foiling operator exists. The heritage and conservation regime actively favours a quiet-mode entrant.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire archipelago lattice — Manda↔Shela (~3 nm), Lamu↔Manda (~2 nm), Lamu↔Kiwayu (~25 nm) — all inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on protected lagoon channel water.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the dense short-hop archipelago electrification playbook the Lamu lattice can plug into at heritage-island scale.

regulatory_note: Kenya Maritime Authority regulates coastal transport. UNESCO World Heritage inscription of Lamu Old Town (2001) plus Kenya Wildlife Service oversight of nearby marine parks (Kiunga Marine National Reserve) gives a strong quiet-mode / conservation anchor. Coastal-security sensitivity historically affected the area but stabilised significantly over the last decade.
seasonality: Year-round; long rains April–May and the SE monsoon (kusi) June–September bring channel chop that the protected lagoon largely shelters from. Peak December–March on the northern hemisphere holiday calendar.

summary: The Lamu Archipelago — Lamu, Manda and Shela islands — is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with sheltered inter-island channels and a dhow-only transport culture. Lamu Old Town allows no motor vehicles, so all access is by boat (dhow, water-taxi). A strong luxury and heritage fit for near-silent foiling that preserves the dhow aesthetic upgrade-path without diesel noise or wake. Discount for remoteness and historical coastal-security sensitivity, but the corridor itself is short, calm, and an ideal premium-resort transfer environment.
tagline: UNESCO heritage archipelago with a dhow-only transport culture — ripe for a silent electric upgrade.
